title: Cohomology of site-perfect field duals
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, $\Lambda=\mathbf F_\ell$, and $T$ a scheme, and $C\in D(T_{et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Assume that an etale covering $\{U_j\to T\}$ makes $C|_{U_j}$ isomorphic to a bounded complex of coefficient sheaves, each term a retract of some finite constant free sheaf $\Lambda_{U_j}^{m}$. This is the ordinary etale predicate DerivedCategory.IsSitePerfect, with no global bound or invertibility assumption. Then for every integer $q$ there is an isomorphism of sheaves $H^q(R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(C,\Lambda_T))\simeq\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(H^{-q}(C),\Lambda_T)$, where the two Hom operations are the derived and ordinary internal Hom of coefficient-module sheaves.

source.place: Local finite-free dual calculation for prime-field site-perfect complexes.

proof.text: On a perfect-model neighborhood the terms are retracts of finite constant free sheaves, hence finite locally constant. Refine the cover to trivialize the finitely many terms and make their differential matrices constant. Thus the whole bounded model comes from a bounded finite-dimensional module complex by the exact strong-monoidal constant-sheaf functor (source CategoryTheory.monoidalConstantSheaf). On bounded finite-free complexes this functor preserves duals: use the strong-monoidal internal-Hom comparison out of a dualizable object (Functor.Monoidal.isIso_ihomComparison_app_of_exactPairing), and exactness commutes with homology. This route uses coefficient-module sheaves directly, with no ringed SheafOfModules bridge.

Apply [lem-pod-cohomology-of-dual-over-field] to the finite-dimensional module model. Over the field the complex splits into its homology and contractible pairs. Evaluation on homology summands is the ordinary duality identity; contractible pairs have zero homology. Mapping this computation through the exact constant-sheaf functor gives the local sheaf-duality formula. The finite-constant ordinary Hom comparison is the same strong-monoidal duality comparison in degree zero.

Construct the canonical comparison from evaluation on Hom cycles and source cycles: the Hom differential shows its value is a coefficient cycle, and changing either argument by a boundary changes the value by a boundary. It therefore descends through both homology quotients, independently of the chosen local models. Exact restriction and evaluation are natural, so these local canonical maps agree on overlaps and descend. The preceding field computation makes them locally invertible; their local inverses also agree. Alternatively test the resulting canonical morphism on geometric stalks and use conservativity. Zero ranks, zero complexes and empty schemes give the zero-object calculation.

lean.statement:
theorem sitePerfect_fieldDual_homology
    (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] (T : Scheme.{u})
    (C : DerivedCategoryModule (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod ℓ)) T) (hC : DerivedCategory.IsSitePerfect C) :
    ∀ q : ℤ, Nonempty
      ((_root_.DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ q).obj
          (((derivedHom (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod ℓ))) T).obj (op C)).obj
            (constantComplex (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod ℓ)) T)) ≅
        (ihom ((_root_.DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ (-q)).obj C)).obj
          (𝟙_ (Sheaf T.smallEtaleTopology
            (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod ℓ))))))
